title: Through Every Age, Eternal God
description: Through Every Age, Eternal God in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 898 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God eternal, and Man mortal. Ps. 90”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Through ev-ery age, e-ter-nal God, Thou art our rest, our safe a-bode! High was thy throne ere heaven was made, Or earth thy hum-ble foot-stool laid.

lines: Thou art our rest, our safe abode!
High was thy throne ere heaven was made,
Or earth thy humble footstool laid.
Long hadst thou reigned ere time began,
Or dust was fashioned into man;
And long thy kingdom shall endure,
When earth and time shall be no more.
A thousand of our years amount
Scarce to a day in thine account;
Or the last watch of ending night.
Sweeps us away; our life's a dream,
An empty tale, a morning flower
Cut down and withered in an hour.

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
